The Trial Chamber accepts the assertions by the Stanisic Defence that the application is based on Rule 66(B), that is, disclosure of items material to the preparation of the Defence, even though Mr. Zecevic has also referred to obligations arising under Rule 68. Indeed, on the 5th of May, Mr. O'Sullivan described the true violation as being of a Rule 66(B) request which was made in January of this year. The jurisprudence relating to Rule 66(B) requires a specific request to be made for disclosure. The Stanisic Defence relies upon its written request to the Prosecution made on the 21st of January which was provided to the Chamber earlier this week. Although various requests had been made earlier than this, Mr. Zecevic acknowledges that a request made in October 2009 was too broad and that the request of the 21st of January, 2011, is the one on which the application is based. The Trial Chamber notes that the letter of the 21st of January refers only to obligations arising under Rule 68 and not to those arising under Rule 66(B). The obligation that's rise under the two rules are different, and in the view of the Trial Chamber, a request specifically referring to obligations under one rule cannot be automatically presumed to include a request under the other. Given Mr. Zecevic's acknowledgment that the previous request made in October 2009 is too broad to meet the requirements of Rule 66(B), it follows that at the time Mr. Bjelosevic commenced his testimony on 12th of April, 2011, no valid request for disclosure under Rule 66(B) had been made to the Prosecution. The oral application for the issue of sanctions against the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68 bis for breach of its obligations under Rule 66(B) must, therefore, fail. The Trial Chamber also notes that the Prosecution has in fact already disclosed a number of the documents in question to the Defence teams and that as a result of the scheduling of this witness, both Defence teams have been on notice of the existence of these documents for at least one month. The Trial Chamber therefore denies the oral application, directs that the Prosecution may use all documents on its list during its cross-examination of this witness. The Trial Chamber remains seized of the written motion of the Stanisic Defence filed on the 28th of April, 2011, to compel the Prosecution to comply with Rule 66(B), which relies on the subsequent request for disclosure under that rule made on the 20th of April, 2011, and the Chamber will address that motion separately. The question which indirectly arises from that, although it's really a separate question, is whether, in light of what the -- movements as we discussed them yesterday and the day before, Mr. Bjelosevic is still expected to continue his cross-examination on Tuesday and not Monday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... to form an understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Your Honours, I'm here to deal with that very topic. As I think you were told by Mr. Hannis yesterday, we were prepared -- I was prepared to continue with my cross-examination even though we didn't have translations of the new material which is now requested by both the Zupljanin and us -- the Zupljanin Defence and us. And I want to return to the question of further cross-examination by Mr. Krgovic. But the reality, I regret to say, is, at the moment, that there are 130 pages of the diary that he produced which, according to CLSS, as estimate today, they cannot do anything before the 24th of May for a draft translation, and final translations until the 27th. Your Honours, we would all like to get on with Mr. Bjelosevic, and I anticipate that if he has to be put off, the Defence will not be able to get another witness here for next week. I'll leave that to the Stanisic Defence to deal with. What we would like is an order from Your Honours, and I think it's a joint order from all concerned, that CLSS is to put everybody that it's got on to doing this so that we could have the translations at the latest -- draft by -- at the latest, by Wednesday of next week. I've certainly got sufficient cross-examination to cover two days without the draft translations. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go on. Desirable though that may be, could we presume to do that, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think Your Honours can say, can make an order that CLSS should devote all its resources to doing this. I really think this has got to get priority. Normally everybody's buried in Karadzic. But as Karadzic isn't sitting at the moment, this should take priority. Your Honours, it's most regrettable that we're in this position. I noted that Mr. Zecevic said yesterday that he wasn't aware that there existed a diary. I find that very difficult to understand, I have to say, because he said relied for the purposes of calling Mr. Bjelosevic on the interview that was conducted with him by the OTP in 2004 when he not only referred to his diary but gave copies of it. And that's what led me to ask for the diary. I somewhat expected that the Defence would produce it through him, but they didn't. And so we made that request. But that's the reality, and it's obviously important. We've had a look through it with the aid of someone who reads the language. Mr. Krgovic and Mr. Zecevic obviously have an advantage that they can read it themselves. And there are entries that are relevant to this case. So, as I say, Your Honour, that's, regrettably, the position. Unless CLSS can have a bomb put under them, if that's the right expression, to get us the translations by Wednesday, we're going to have a problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Korner. My impression yesterday, and I may have gotten it wrong or the situation may have changed, is that -- and this is when Mr. Hannis was addressing us, is that, from the OTP's understanding of the contents of this diary, you would have been in a position to begin and then the -- see where we go with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Was that premised on the assumption that you would get the translation in the course of the week?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It has to be. Your Honours, I mean, I -- much, though, and I say, I could probably spend ten days cross-examining this man. I don't think that's really a proper way of going about it. I could -- I was -- we were working on the premise that we'd get the translations this week. I've certainly got sufficient to deal with. But if we can't get the translations for the 24th, which is, I think it's the middle of next week, isn't it? The 24th. Tuesday week, yes. That -- that -- then -- that will stop -- bring things to a halt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, the -- you were going to make another point about Mr. Krgovic's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I noted that Mr. Krgovic got to his feet and said that he wanted to do 30 more minutes' cross-examination. And the same principles apply to Mr. Krgovic, who presumably knew that Mr. Bjelosevic had handed over, as it were, already a huge number of documents to the Defence that we didn't know about and took no action at that stage to see if there were any other documents he wanted to get. Your Honours, although I -- we could object in its entirety to Mr. Krgovic re-opening his cross-examination, we don't do that. But we do say, and we submit to Your Honours, that he must be limited in further cross-examination. Because I've begun my cross-examination. And clearly if he's going to be allowed to do it, he should do it now. But it has to be limited to topics he raised originally. He cannot open, we would submit, any new topics in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought it would have been confined to the diary, what was revealed in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no. The diary, Your Honours, he can only use the diary, we would submit, for further cross if it relates to topics that he raised already in cross-examination. He cannot then go off and do a whole new series of topics and therefore continue his cross-examination. He's finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Aren't you anticipating, Ms. Korner? Because it may very well be that, upon an examination, that there are areas which he hadn't previously explored but which, in the light of what the diaries show, ought to be explored.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no, Your Honour, well, that's the whole point. That's what I'm objecting to. He had the opportunity himself to obtain from Mr. Bjelosevic the diary if he thought it was going to be of relevance. He should not be allowed to go into a whole new series of questions because we have asked for this diary. He cannot just re-open his cross-examination like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suspect that the -- such objections are going to have be addressed as and when they rise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, no, I think Your Honours -- I'm sorry, but I think Your Honours can say - there has to be a limit - if there are matters which he has already addressed, topics which are -- on which the diary he thinks assists him, that's one matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You may be correct, and we may come to agree with you, Ms. Korner. It's just that we're not prepared to deal with that and to rule today. We want to think about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in that event, then I'll leave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... so to come --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At least Mr. Krgovic knows our position on this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So to come back to -- sorry, Mr. Krgovic, you wanted to say something on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to make things easier for the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor. When I asked for additional cross-examination, I just wanted to ask the witness about the topics that I had already asked him about and in connection with which documents have appeared in the mean time. In my cross-examination, I'm not going to go beyond the topics that I already asked him about. That is to say, I'm not going to raise new topics.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but, Your Honours, that also raises the next problem. Mr. Krgovic should do his cross-examination first thing on Tuesday. He's asked for certain entries to be translated so he can use them. So unless we can get a guarantee from CLSS that at the very least those will be available by -- well, I suppose by Monday, really, then I'm not sure whether we're going on Tuesday either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You said first thing on Tuesday. What I assume you mean is that he should begin his cross-examination before you resume yours. Whenever that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I think that that is the ruling of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But he can't do that because he won't have the entries translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I was about to say that I am going to attempt to formulate an order for adjournment. And, please, I invite counsel and indeed my fellow Judges to jump in if it could be made clearer. In the light of what has been said, upon the rising of the Court, we will resume on Tuesday. But this is subject to communication being made by e-mail, I suppose, if the progress on the translation of the diaries make a Tuesday resumption impractical.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours it -- undoubtedly it will be impractical unless Your Honours can make some kind of a -- if not an order to CLSS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we will, of course, make the necessary inquiries. The problems, as you would very well appreciate, Ms. Korner, with judicial orders is that there is no point in making orders that cannot be enforced.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And therein lies the problem for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, and I'm told, hopefully, that the -- Mr. Krgovic has requested simply seven pages. So at least we hope that CLSS would be able to complete those seven pages on Monday. And then see where we go. The other problem, of course, is that Mr. Bjelosevic will be travelling on Monday, and it's not going to be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: What the Chamber will do is rise at this point. And rather than adjourning for the day, we would explore all of the things that need to be explored and come back into court in -- at 12.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, could you assist us? The six pages that -- to which you had referred, had they been tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. I used them during my cross-examination. And my mistake, I should have immediately sought an application to tender them then. And I just reminded Your Honours at the end of all of the evidence that I do seek to tender those six pages. The -- it's just the introduction to the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we have a tab number or a 65 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. 65 ter 20081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 81. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tab 16. It's the introduction "Anthropogeographic Reality of Serbs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So it's admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 20081 will become Exhibit P2322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have, during the break, made such inquiries as we could, and there are a number of options which present themselves. But one of the questions that would be useful for us is whether the Prosecution could indicate immediately, ideally, or in the course of today, whether the -- they're in a position to identify a reasonable number of pages, and I'm not going to give a number, which CLSS might be -- which they propose that CLSS might be able to produce by the middle of next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They say -- what would a reasonable number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to avoid saying. Let me hear what you're offering.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's a bit like a . Your Honours, we've identified, I think, between all of us, something like 130 pages of which were the greatest sinners, as it were, for the amount we want in. I cannot give an answer off the top of my head which we say are, for example, picking a figure out of the air, the most vital 20. I would need to go back and go through it with those who speak B/C/S who have gone through it already. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: A maximum of 50, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We might be able to live with that, Your Honours. And if anything comes up during the course of it, even if we don't have a translation we can always put up the B/C/S on the screen. They're all, I understand, pretty short entries. They're not pages and pages, so -- but that -- we'll go through that this afternoon and we'll give a list, and we'll make sure that CLSS gets the list this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Incidentally one of the questions that came up is whether OTP had begun the process of transcribing, what I assume is a manuscript, into a -- to facilitate the work of CLSS. Do you know off the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you mean putting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] To type out the manuscript. Type up the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. No. No, Your Honours. I mean, if you take -- we've had people looking at it. We got the documents on -- and we haven't done anything like that. It's handwritten. That's simply not a job we could do in advance of giving this to CLSS. So I hear -- so I can see that will cause a slight problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, this seems to allow us - and tell me if I'm wrong - to start on Tuesday with Mr. Krgovic's 30 minutes' cross-examination. By the way, Mr. Krgovic, you should provide CLSS with the seven pages you need so -- today so that they can translate that for Tuesday, or -- for Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I help. Mr. Krgovic sent the ERN numbers to us yesterday, and we've put in the request to CLSS already, and we'll make sure that they prioritise those seven pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. They just told us they didn't know yet. But perhaps that's a misunderstanding. So if that's the case, could we then start on Tuesday, have two days of your examination not related to the new material, have the first maximum 50 pages ready for you by mid week, and that means that Tuesday, when, Thursday you could go on with the new material.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm perfectly content with that. I can certainly cross-examine on the material we've already put in, Tuesday, Wednesday, and probably Thursday. So provided we can get such material as we need by Friday, that should be ample. As I say, we'll just have to hope that 50 pages will cover it all. Your Honours, can I just ask this, and this is an order Your Honours can make, although it's been discussed, I think it needs an order from Your Honours. Would Your Honours order that when Mr. Bjelosevic returns he brings with him the original of the diary which he photocopied, the original of his military booklet, and also - and I'm sorry to have to ask you this, but there's a very good reason for it - any other diary he kept during the period of meetings he attended. Just the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So it's more precise not only a diary that you're referring to, but a diary of meeting he attended?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If he has in his possession any other diary which records meetings that he attended during the period October 1991 to December 1992, would he also be kind enough to bring the original of that with him on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there any reason why the Chamber shouldn't make the order as now prayed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the VWS would see the -- from the transcript, the terms of the order which the Chamber now makes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And are any other housekeeping matters before we rise?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In which case, we would resume at 9.00 on Tuesday morning. Thank you. I trust everybody has a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of May, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.35 p.m.,
